title: "To Be That Self Which One Truly Is": A Therapist's View of Personal Goals
coreMove: Translate a borrowed goal into the more truthful self-contact it is trying to avoid or protect.
sourcePressure: The chapter defines personal goals around congruence and real selfhood rather than compliance with borrowed ideals. Frozen sidecar ch08 supports the heading, part placement, and broad thematic claims; it exposes no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning self-acceptance into passivity or modern true-self rhetoric.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of personal goals
